data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim's first two sentences are correct, but its last sentence is wrong. The ADBMS1818 Rev. B ordering guide (p. 92) assigns ASWAZ, ASWAZ-R7 and ASWAZ-RL to SW-64-2 and ASWZ, ASWZ-R7 and ASWZ-RL to 05-08-1982. Both outlines are 64-lead LQFP_EP, with a 10.00 mm body, 12.00 mm across the leads and a 0.50 mm pitch. The exposed pad is 5.74 ±0.10 mm in 05-08-1982 (Figure 113, p. 91) and 5.50 mm SQ (5.40 to 5.60) in SW-64-2 (Figure 114, p. 92). The LTC6813-1 Rev. B datasheet, p. 88, puts every LWE part on 'Reference LTC DWG #05-08-1982 Rev A'. That includes LTC6813HLWE-1#3ZZPBF and #3ZZTRPBF. So these two LTC6813 rows share the ASWZ outline, 05-08-1982. JLCPCB reports 350 in stock (presale 337) for C2758259 and 270 in stock (presale 247) for C2979142. Both pass the stock gate: S4 at 5 boards × 1 placement gives 25, so the floor of 50 applies. The re-rank's scratch directory holds readings of both rows. ADBMS1818ASWZ-RL (C2971928, 2723 in stock) is also in 05-08-1982. Whichever row is Rank 2, the shortlist therefore holds more than one row in the outline that is not Rank 1's, and 'Rank 2 is the only shortlist row in the other outline' is false. Separately, JLCPCB labels C2979142 'LQFP-64(10x10)' with no EP. That contradicts the datasheet, which counts. This ruling is about the report's figure for this function, not about the ADBMS1818 part itself. Not read: the text of the re-rank report is not on disk, so the shortlist membership comes from the verifier's quotation of the report section 'shortlist JLCPCB stock' and from the re-rank's scratch readings (/home/claude/rcbench-research/round1/scratch/T4/rerank-R9/jlc_C2758259.json, jlc_C2979142.json).
